source_document.body:
Photo: rPlus Energies
The US has installed more than 200 gigawatt-hours (GWh) of battery storage, with nearly 50 GWh coming online in the first nine months of 2026 alone.
The US added 48.3 GWh of battery storage through September, up 20% from the same stretch last year, according to the latest report from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA) and Benchmark Mineral Intelligence. Q3 was a little slower: The US installed 14.3 GWh in those three months, down 1% year over year.
Texas is in the lead
Texas added 12.3 GWh of grid-scale batteries through September, more than any other state. Arizona came in second at 7.7 GWh, followed by California at 6.8 GWh. And 11 states had already broken their annual storage installation records with three months to go – Colorado, Massachusetts, Utah, Michigan, Georgia, Mississippi, Virginia, Iowa, Montana, Alabama, and Illinois.
Utility-scale batteries did most of the work in Q3, accounting for 12.2 GWh of new capacity. Businesses and industrial sites added another 1.3 GWh, and residential added 746 megawatt-hours (MWh). That was the best Q3 yet for home batteries, though installs through September were still down 12% year over year. Some homeowners moved up their installations last year before the federal residential clean energy tax credit ended.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
“States are moving from targets to centralized procurements,” said Pete Tillotson, a senior analyst at Benchmark. In September, New York awarded contracts for eight battery projects that can deliver about 950 megawatts (MW) combined. SEIA and Benchmark now expect 708 GWh of storage across the grid, homes, and businesses by 2030, up 3.7% from their previous forecast.
The US can also make more battery cells here. A Tennessee factory opened in July and an Indiana factory opened in October, bringing US cell manufacturing capacity to 92.4 GWh, up 50%.
What about people’s electric bills?
Solar and batteries helped bring down average summer wholesale power prices by 42% in Texas’s ERCOT market and 51% in California’s CAISO market between 2021 and 2026, according to SEIA’s inflation-adjusted analysis . When batteries had power to spare during peak hours, grid operators could call on expensive power plants less often.
You wouldn’t know it from looking at the total on residential electric bills. The cost of generating power for households fell in both markets, but the cost of delivering it to homes rose. Overall, residential bills rose 22% at the two California utilities SEIA examined and 3% across its Texas utility sample, driven by higher transmission and distribution costs. California is upgrading its grid to reduce the risk of wildfires. Texas is expanding its grid for rising demand and make it more resilient to storms.
More than 300 solar and battery storage companies in the US wrote to Congress last week asking it to pass the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. SEIA CEO Tim Pawlenty says the permitting bill would help get projects built faster and ease pressure on power prices. However, many Democrats feel this bill falls short. The Senate voted 70–27 on Monday to end debate on the amendment containing the bill’s text, moving it closer to a final vote.

He Bought a BMW M3 CS and Parked It, Then Listed It for Sale a Month Later
43 photos
Photo: Cars and Bids
Sometimes it's incompatibility. Other times, it's about some other car. And other times it is just about cashing in. Those are some of the reasons why people end up listing for sale the car that they just bought. This is one of those stories. The original owner bought this 2027 BMW M3 CS Handschalter in October 2026. A month later, it is already for sale.
This BMW checks all the right boxes. Well, of course, if you like the “beaver teeth.” I, for one, must admit that it is starting to grow on me, especially when it comes with the red border trim and black-and-red “M3 CS” badging. Right, busted, guilty pleasure! Aside from that, there is really nothing to point out as an obvious flaw on this M3.
It is an M3 CS, which stands for Competition Sport, but you might as well pretend it stands for "Constant Sliding," because that is exactly what happens in the millisecond you turn off traction control on a damp track. Whatever you go for, this car sure sounds like fun from bumper to bumper.
Then, just look at it. It is finished in the showstopping Isle of Man Green Metallic, which looks just as good as Twilight Purple Pearl, over an Anthracite interior with M Carbon bucket seats and Merino leather upholstery. The car rides on lightweight forged Style 827M wheels, measuring 19 inches up front and 20 inches out back.
Photo: Cars and Bids This BMW M3 CS has the wheels finished in matte black, but the other option would have been matte gold bronze, which would have surely been a bit too much. The hood features two distinct recessed stripes left unpainted to show off the exposed carbon weave underneath because this car comes with tons (it’s a metaphor, not actual tons!) of carbon fiber.
The car comes with the Handschalter designation, which is German for "hand shifter." I told you it checks all the right boxes. That six-speed manual transmission puts down what the twin-turbocharged 3.0-liter straight-six pushes out through the rear wheels. Told you it’s built in the name of fun!
That would be 473 horsepower (480 metric horsepower) and 406 pound-feet (550 Newton meters) of torque, which is enough to make it rocket from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph) in 4.1 seconds and top out at 180 mph (290 kph) when the M Driver's Package is involved. Every single M3 CS Handschalter leaves the factory with the package.
However, the original owner didn’t enjoy much of that performance. He listed the 2027 BMW M3 CS Handschalter for sale with just 68 miles (109 kilometers) on the clock, which is basically delivery mileage and driving around the block a couple of times.
Photo: Cars and Bids The manual BMW M3 CS is so cool that even Doug DeMuro, who reviewed it, said he wanted it. " I considered calling @Cargovoyage and telling him that I was keeping it, " he wrote in the comments section of the listing.
" Go for it, Doug! " the seller replied. However, DeMuro has just bought a 2006 Ford GT Heritage Edition for an undisclosed price, soon after selling his Midnight Blue 2005 Ford GT “never liked the color” non-Heritage Edition for $540,000, so he might not be in the market for another car just yet.
The still-new manual BMW is part of a special production run rolled out in very limited numbers, exclusive to North America . BMW hasn't indicated the exact number of units to be produced, but dealer allocation reports indicate a production of roughly 640 to 740 units.
It comes with carbon fiber components all over, such as carbon ceramic brakes and a carbon fiber roof panel, along with unique chassis tuning, which shaves off 75 pounds (34 kilograms) of the weight of the standard M3 in this spec.
Photo: Cars and Bids Because removing the front-axle all-wheel-drive system frees up clearance, the BMW M3 CS Handschalter with rear-wheel drive sits a quarter of an inch (6 millimeters) closer to the pavement compared to the standard M3.
The future owner is getting a brand-new car, which hasn’t even required service yet, with a gorgeous spec and no need to wait for months to have it delivered, along with two keys, the owner’s manual, the window sticker, and the wheel lock key.
The original owner paid $119,150 to drive this BMW off the showroom floor. Now, with six days to go, the most generous offer out of the 13 bids already placed is inching closer to the sticker and will most likely go way past it. Right now, it sits at $113,476 and counting.
" All that money for a car that'll get walked on by a Tesla Model 3 Performance, " someone wrote in the comments section. But the Model 3 Performance has no Isle of Man paint and definitely no manual transmission. There is no comparison between the two for a real car enthusiast.
This purchase and sale after just one month of ownership is starting to look every inch like a tutorial about cashing in. However, surprisingly, nobody asked the seller why he is selling so fast.

Toyota is recalling 19,000 electric C-HR SUVs globally, with about 10,000 affected in the US.
Toyota C-HR EV recall expands globally
In September, Toyota issued a safety recall involving certain model-year 2026 C-HR electric SUVs in North America.
Toyota initially said about 10,000 models were involved, but later confirmed the number was 8,521 in a letter to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA).
According to Germany’s federal motor authority, Kraftfahrt-Bundesamt (KBA), the recall has now expanded to 19,000 C-HR vehicles globally. In Germany, the recall impacts 1,096 vehicles and is still under investigation by the KBA.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
The issue stems from faulty software programming in the EV-ECU. While it’s intended to limit the battery’s charge level, the software can cause it to overcharge under certain conditions.
Toyota said the issue occurs if the battery is already at a high state of charge and the driver continues using the regenerative braking system.
When this happens, warning lights and a sound will alert the driver, and the electric drive system can shut down, causing the vehicle to lose power while driving.
Toyota C-HR EV (Source: Toyota)
Following an internal investigation, Toyota said in the NHTSA report that the issue was caused by incorrect software that disrupted the charging-limit function, allowing the battery to overcharge while driving.
The Toyota C-HR vehicles included in the recall were produced between June 17, 2025, and July 9, 2026.
In Europe and other overseas markets, Toyota sells the C-HR EV as the C-HR+ to distinguish it from the gas- or hybrid-powered version.
Toyota C-HR XSE interior (Source: Toyota)
Owners of affected vehicles in North America can take them to a Toyota dealership, where the battery ECU software will be updated free of charge.
Toyota mailed owner notification letters out on October 18, 2026. Owners can contact Toyota’s customer service at 1-800-331-4331. The recall number is 26TA17.
Other than saying the EV-ECU is being reprogrammed, Toyota has not yet announced next steps for owners of affected vehicles outside North America. The KBA reference number is 17116R.
Check back for more details. The recall only affects the 2026 C-HR. The 2027 Toyota C-HR is also now on sale.

reference.quote: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd restore Asia-Europe Suez routes as U.S. shippers watch capacity and costs

context_references.quote: Maersk and Hapag-Lloyd restore Asia-Europe Suez routes as U.S. shippers watch capacity and costs

source_document.body:
A contract dispute involving about 250 union watchmen could disrupt cargo movement at the ports of Los Angeles and Long Beach as early as this Saturday , with the Pacific Maritime Association reporting little progress in the latest negotiations with International Longshore and Warehouse Union Local 26.
According to a statement Wednesday from the PMA, talks ended Tuesday with little to no movement from the union on the employer association’s proposals. The ILWU has already held a strike vote and has indicated it is unwilling to extend its contract beyond its expiration at 12:01 a.m. Saturday, PMA said.
The two sides are scheduled to return to the bargaining table Friday, leaving a narrow window to reach an agreement before the deadline.
Concerns are heightened that ILWU dockworkers would honor pickets set up by the watchmen, all but shutting down some cargo operations.
Employers said its offer includes a one-time $3,200 bonus for each local member and a wage proposal that would increase average annual earnings for full-time watchmen from more than $170,000 to $198,000.
The proposal would also maintain fully employer-paid healthcare for active workers and retirees, which PMA values at more than $62,000 annually, and increase annual pension benefits to as much as $93,200 for workers with the longest tenure.
PMA said negotiations have continued for more than a year, most recently with assistance from the Federal Mediation and Conciliation Service. The association said it secured a several-week contract extension to allow further negotiations, but that the union participated in bargaining on only three days during that extension.
The association also said Local 26’s demands have not materially changed since negotiations began.
FreightWaves has reached out to the union for comment.
Local 26 represents unarmed watchmen who perform security duties at six container terminals across the two ports. Their work includes checking identification and credentials at terminal entrances, conducting routine patrols and reporting security or safety concerns.
Although the watchmen account for about 2% of the ports’ ILWU workforce, PMA said the terminals where they work handle more than half of the two ports’ combined cargo, including roughly 85% of cargo at Long Beach and 33% at Los Angeles.
PMA expects thousands of longshore workers, marine clerks and foremen who are not involved in the contract dispute to honor a Local 26 picket line. That could significantly expand the effects of a watchmen’s strike, interrupting cargo handling well beyond the bargaining unit itself.
Potential consequences include idle truck drivers, disrupted rail shipments and reduced hours for warehouse workers. Exporters, including farmers and manufacturers, could face shipping delays, while retailers and small businesses preparing for the holidays could encounter delayed deliveries and higher costs.
Employers quoted data from maritime and aviation analyst Martin Associates that found the six terminals where Local 26 members work handled about 6.2 million containers in 2025, generating 50,000 direct jobs and supporting nearly 4.2 million jobs nationwide.
The analysis linked that cargo volume to $885 billion in national economic activity, $48 billion in federal taxes and $190 billion in personal income.
Martin warned that losses would grow exponentially the longer a strike continued, as vessels could not be unloaded and containers already inside terminals could not be cleared.
Why it matters: The dispute’s potential impact extends far beyond the roughly 250 watchmen negotiating a contract. If other dockworkers honor picket lines, a strike could interrupt terminals handling a substantial share of cargo at the nation’s busiest port complex, with effects cascading through the supply chain.

1952 Packard-Henney Junior Is a Former USAF Ambulance, Also a Rare Prototype
17 photos
Photo: Mecum Auctions
Packard is mainly known for luxury vehicles, but some of its chassis also found their way into hearses and ambulances. And although they may not be as desirable as the civilian cars, these professional vehicles are much rarer. This 1952 Packard-Henney Junior is one of them.
The Junior isn't a nameplate but a term that designated Packard's more accessible models, such as the One-Twenty, the 115C, or the Clipper . This ambulance is based on the latter, which had been revived in the early 1950s after a six-year absence from dealerships.
It was built by the Henney Motor Company, which started out as a carriage builder and joined the professional car market in 1916. From 1937 to 1954, Henney produced ambulances and hearses based on Packard chassis exclusively. The company went out of business in 1954, when Packard merged with Studebaker.
Smaller than regular professional vehicles built on longer wheelbase cars, the Junior was supposed to attract customers through its maneuverability and fuel economy. However, the line wasn't very successful, with Henney selling only about 620 examples through 1954. And because many of these vehicles were scrapped or abandoned after a few years on the road, they're quite hard to find nowadays.
Back in 2022, I showed you a video of two Juniors resting in a warehouse . They were the first Henney ambulances I had seen in several years. Well, the one you see here may very well be the finest example in existence. It popped up among the lots for Mecum's Kissimmee 2027 auction. It's in excellent condition, and it's also rarer than the average Junior.
That's because it's one of the three prototypes that Henney put together in 1952. And it's believed to be the only known surviving example. Moreover, it was originally used by the United States Air Force, serving for about three years at the Barksdale base, in Louisiana.
The vehicle was retired from military service in 1957, with only 30,000 miles (48,280 km) on the odometer. It was then stored at a military surplus yard in Hot Springs, Arkansas, for about 40 years. The car sat under a cover.
In the late 1990s, the ambulance was sold at a government auction and went back in storage. In 2017, it was then purchased by Packard enthusiast Pat Turano, who displayed it at several events and car shows, including the Lake Mirror Classic Concours in Florida.
There's no mentioning of a restoration, so this Packard is most likely an unrestored survivor. It will cross the block with documents from Barksdale Air Force Base, a period yearbook, a Packard-branded fire extinguisher, and lots of military memorabilia. The seller also included a period-correct US military stretcher, a technical sergeant's khaki shirt and service cap, as well as a military first aid kit box.
The gavel will fall on January 7, 2027 . Mecum has yet to publish an estimated price, but the Packard will have a reserve. How much do you think it will go for?

This Tuned Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren Will Annoy Purists. But It’s Not Real
11 photos
Photo: Instagram | onb.artdesign
Every gearhead and their grandmother will recognize the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren in a sea of supercars, and that’s despite the fact that this exotic model hasn’t been a thing since 2010.
Production spanned from 2003 to 2010, and it is estimated that over 2,000 examples saw the light of day during this time. All of them were made at McLaren’s factory in Woking, UK. Gordon Murray and Gorden Wagener were responsible with the design, and the model was offered as a two-door coupe and a two-door roadster. The speedster (Stirling Moss) joined them, and all had a front mid-engine and rear-wheel drive layout.
Due to the layout, the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren is more of an exotic grand tourer rather than a full-blown supercar, but it’s definitely not wrong to refer to it by using the latter term. After all, just look at it! Hasn’t it aged perfectly? It certainly has, this writer thinks, and given the face that it is an automotive icon, purists will be annoyed by the fact that some copies have been visited by the tuning fairy, including the one pictured above.
Or has it? Actually, this is nothing more than a mere rendering take on the model, which features a few modifications. The front bumper is new, and it is bigger than the OEM one. It features some flicks, as well as a splitter. The hood has also been tweaked, there is new trim on the front fenders, and we can also see new side skirt attachments.
Photo: Instagram | onb.artdesign Fender flares are part of the CGI makeover, and this Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren also features a new rear bumper, a diffuser, and a giant wing attached to the trunk lid. The ducktail spoiler is also new, and so other other bits and bobs on the outside. The wheels are significantly larger than the OEM ones, and we can see that the tailpipe trim is also on the fresh side of things.
The cockpit hasn’t opened up to the camera, but believe us when we tell you that while it definitely shows its age, it is not bad at all. Some will argue that the quality of materials is on a next level compared to today’s Mercedes cars, but that’s a topic for another time.
Meanwhile, we will wrap it up by reminding you that the Mercedes-Benz SLR McLaren features a supercharged 5.4-liter V8 engine, making 617 hp (460 kW/626 ps) in the regular variant, with superior models having 641 hp (478 kW/650 ps) available via the right pedal. A five-speed automatic transmission delivered the power to the rear wheels.
The SLR took around 3.5 seconds to hit 60 mph (97 kph) in independent tests, and could keep pushing up to 208 mph (334 kph). Not bad for a ride that’s more than two decades old, is it? View this post on Instagram A post shared by Onur Bakır (@onb.artdesign)

Ford Ranger in Danger? Vietnamese Firm Rolls Out the $33,000 Wild Pickup Truck
7 photos
Photo: VinFast
While the Chinese are struggling to make their way into the United States, Vietnam has the doors wide open and rolls out yet another model. This time, it is giving the Ford Ranger a run for its money, transforming the segment into a battleground of styles and powertrains with its latest VF Wild. A planned factory in North Carolina, currently slated for 2028 at the earliest, was supposed to help them position their models more competitively.
While America is trying to keep Chinese cars at bay, the Vietnamese seem to be going all in. VinFast’s Wild is ready to take on the Ford Maverick, Ranger, and upcoming Fathom, as well as Slate’s pickup truck. The United States has locked the Chinese out of the country with massive tariffs and restrictions on connected vehicles, software, and hardware linked to China.
But VinFast comes all the way from Vietnam to steal the show from popular or expected-to-become-popular pickup trucks. The Wild has just hit its home market, Vietnam, with a starting price of 860 million VND, which translates to roughly $33,000, Autoblog reports . To keep up with the East, Ford is already working on another affordable pickup truck, set to be launched after the arrival of the Fathom.
That would place it right beside the Ford Ranger , which starts around $33,500. It would be more expensive than the Maverick (around $28,145) and the upcoming Fathom ($28,350), while the Slate truck is the most affordable of the pack at $24,950.
Photo: VinFast The concept that previewed the model was electric, but the VinFast VF Wild strays away from its all-electric roots. Instead, it features a 1.5-liter range extender and an electric motor that produces 215 horsepower (218 metric horsepower).
The 46.4 kWh LFP battery stores enough energy for a drive of up to 155 miles (250 kilometers) on electric power only before the truck needs to be plugged in again. The Wild can roll up to 620 miles (1,000 kilometers) with the tank and battery full.
The battery supports 6.6 kW AC charging and up to 90 kW DC fast charging, taking 30 to 32 minutes to charge from 10% to 70%. It also includes Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) technology to power external tools and camping appliances.
The model measures 211.6 inches (5,376 millimeters) in length, which means it is slightly longer than Ford’s Ranger (210.6 inches or 5,349 millimeters) and far larger than the Maverick (199.7 inches or 5,072 millimeters). The numbers make it slightly larger than both of Ford’s entry-level pickups.
Photo: VinFast The VF Wild comes with a payload of 1,653 pounds (750 kilograms), which is very similar to that of the Ford Ranger: 1,711 pounds (776 kilograms). The Vietnamese truck’s towing capacity has yet to be announced. Unlike the Ford Ranger, the Wild is 2WD only.
The Wild features a minimalist interior, with a 10-inch touchscreen that controls most of the vehicle’s onboard functions, and reclining second-row seats to maximize passenger space. Just like the Tesla Model 3 and VinFast VF 3, the VF Wild ditches the traditional driver instrument cluster and head-up display.
The gear selector sits on a stalk behind the flat-bottomed steering wheel, freeing up space on the center console for storage compartments and cupholders. Built-in tech includes a contextual voice assistant, over-the-air firmware updates, battery health monitoring, and remote vehicle controls via smartphone or smartwatch apps.
VinFast has not announced an official U.S. release date for the VF Wild, and it may not arrive in America until 2028 or later. VinFast only sells two electric SUVs in the United States: the VF 8 , which starts at $41,790 with the destination fees included, and the six- or seven-seat VF 9, which costs $64,290.
Photo: VinFast For the VF 8, the price includes a complimentary VinFast home charger and VinFast e-bike, alongside 0% APR financing offers for up to 84 months. The automaker has delayed the smaller VF 6 and VF 3, while the VF 3, already delayed multiple times, should arrive in the United States as a tiny, two-door micro-SUV, expected to kick off at under $20,000. For the moment, the model remains on indefinite hold for the U.S. market.
Every VinFast sold in America is currently imported from Hai Phong, Vietnam. Without a U.S. assembly plant, bringing a pickup like the VF Wild to America would trigger the 25% "Chicken Tax" applied to foreign-built light trucks (pickup trucks and cargo vans. This would make it nearly impossible for the firm to price it competitively.
To offset tariffs, VinFast is planning to build a plant in Moncure, North Carolina. Originally scheduled to open in July 2024 and later pushed to 2026, the plant was rescheduled to start operating in 2028 at the earliest, as the company cited slow U.S. EV demand.
Aside from clearing and grading the 1,765-acre site, VinFast has not erected any factory buildings. Furthermore, in May 2026, North Carolina Attorney General Jeff Jackson sued VinFast for breaching its development contract.
